units.title: Basic of Electricity and Auxiliaries system. 1.a State importance and significance of basic electrical principles.
topics: 1.1. Basic electrical principles -Effects of current flow, and definition of electrical quantities like resistance, voltage, current, and power. -Differences between Conductors, insulators and semiconductors, -Basics of Magnetism, electromagnetism, Electromagnetic induction, Mutual induction. - Differences between electron flow and conventional flow.
1.2. Fundamentals of automotive wiring, terminals, cables, color codes, harness design, fuses, relay and circuit breakers, and switches.
1.3. Construction and working of various electrical auxiliaries systems – -Windscreen washers and wipers, - Signaling circuits, - Horns, - Engine cooling fan motors, - electric window
1.4. Construction and working of analog and digital gauges such as - Tachometers, - Odometers, - Speedometers, - Oil pressure gauges, - Coolant temperature gauge, - Fuel level gauge.

1.5. Automotive Lighting fundamentals, - Bulbs, - Headlight reflectors, - Headlight lenses, - Basic lighting circuit, Automobile Electrical and Electronic System Course Code: 4330203 - Gas discharge lamps and - LED lighting.

units.title: Automotive battery 2.a Explain construction and working of automotive batteries. 2.b Explain battery disposal and handling procedure.
topics: 2.1. Vehicle batteries Various types of battery, Requirements of the vehicle battery, Choosing the correct battery, parameters affecting battery performance.
2.2. Lead-acid batteries Construction, working, chemical reaction during charging and discharging, Battery rating and efficiency,
2.3. Lithium-ion batteries Construction, working, comparison between lead acid batteries and lithium- ion batteries.
2.4. lead–acid battery Waste, battery disposal, battery handling and storage.

units.title: Ignition system 3.a Explain construction and working of various Ignition system. 3.b Describe various types of spark plug and rating.
topics: 3.1. Necessity and requirement of Ignition system in automobile vehicles.
3.2. Construction and working of breaker point ignition system, electronic ignition system and distributor less ignition system.
3.3. Construction, working and types of Spark plugs.
3.4. Working of Non–Contact–type Ignition Triggering devices.
3.5. Construction and working of Capacitive Discharge Ignition.

units.title: Starting and charging system 4.a Explain construction and working of different starting system. 4.b Describe necessity and
topics: 4.1. Necessity and requirements of the starting system.
4.2. Basic working of Starting system circuits.
4.3. Describe D.C motor characteristics.
4.4. Constructional and working principle of different starter motor - Pre-engaged starters, - Permanent magnet starters, - Various drive mechanisms of starter motor.

4.5. Necessity and requirements of the charging system - Basic operating principles, Automobile Electrical and Electronic System Course Code: 4330203 - Alternator characteristics, - Construction and working of Alternator, - Requirement of regulators, - Working of regulators.

units.title: Automotive Electronics 5.a State importance and significance of electronics components and circuits. 5.b Explain the concepts of ECU in a...
topics: 5.1. Electronic components and circuits introduction, components, electronics symbols, Integrated circuits, Amplifiers, Bridge circuits, Digital-to-analogue conversion, Analogue-to-digital conversion, Logic gates, Combinational logic, Timers and counters, Memory circuits, Clock, or a stable circuit
5.2. Microprocessor systems Introduction, Ports, Central processing unit (CPU), Memory, Buses, A typical microprocessor, Microcontrollers

5.3. Construction, working and use of various Sensors -Thermistors, -Thermocouples, -Inductive sensors, -Hall Effect, -Strain gauges, -Various Variable capacitance sensors, -Accelerometer (knock sensors), -LVDT, RVDT, -various flow sensors, -Optical sensors, -Light sensors, -Thick-film air temperature sensor, -Methanol sensor, -Rain sensor, -Oil sensor, -Dynamic vehicle position sensors.

5.4. Construction, working and use of Actuators -Solenoid actuators, -Motorized actuators, -Stepper motors, -Synchronous motors, -Thermal actuators. Note: The UOs need to be formulated at the ‘Application Level’ and above of Revised Bloom’s Taxonomy’ to accelerate the attainment of the COs and the competency.
